newsitem.title: USA: White House sees tobacco deal long way off.
newsitem.headline: White House sees tobacco deal long way off.

text.p: The White House said Monday a tobacco settlement proposal seems to be a long way off.
Spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters the White House was actively monitoring the settlement talks between negotiators for state attorneys general and the tobacco industry.

About 30 states are suing cigarette makers to recover Medicaid money spent on treating smoking-related illnesses. The industry wants protection from legal damages but the attorneys general are reluctant to give tobacco companies the immunity from lawsuits they seek.
McCurry essentially agreed with Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala, who warned negotiators not to expect the White House to sign off immediately on any deal.
He said any deal "is going to require a very careful review" with an eye toward ensuring "the best possible public health outcome."
"At the moment, as near as we can tell publicly judging from the comments of the parties themselves, we're a long way from having that question before us in any event," McCurry said.
